inputs.content:
# Brightwork: should we launch an AI dispatch assistant? — briefing pack

> **Synthetic benchmark data.** The company, people, competitors and every figure in this pack are fictional. They were generated for a reasoning benchmark and are internally consistent, but they are not real market data.

## 1. Context

Brightwork sells field-service management software (scheduling, dispatch, quotes, invoicing) to HVAC,
plumbing and electrical contractors with 3–50 technicians. It has 9,800 customer accounts with an average of
6.2 office seats each (dispatchers and office staff) on the Core plan at $79 per seat per month: annual recurring
revenue (ARR) of $57.6M. Gross margin is 78%, annual logo churn 14%, net revenue retention 101%.

The product team has built **Dispatch Copilot**: AI that proposes a day's schedule, drafts quotes from
technician notes, and summarises customer calls. It ran as a free beta for 12 weeks.

**Decision maker:** CEO Maya Okafor and the executive team, at January 2027 planning.

## 2. Decision question

**Should Brightwork launch Dispatch Copilot in Q2 2027, and if so, how should it be packaged and priced?**

## 3. Objectives and constraints

- Raise net revenue retention from 101% to 105% by 2028.
- Keep company gross margin at or above 75%.
- Engineering: 60 engineers in total. Launching Copilot needs 14 engineers for two quarters, which delays the
  rewrite of the technician mobile app by two quarters.

## 4. Current view inside the company

The Chief Product Officer proposes launching Copilot as a **paid add-on at $149 per account per month**: "Our
survey shows 46% of customers are likely to buy it. That is about $8M of new ARR in the first year."
The Head of Customer Success worries about the mobile app delay: "Mobile reliability is what customers complain
about."

## 5. Beta results (240 accounts, 12 weeks, volunteers)

**Table 1. Beta outcomes**

| Measure | Beta accounts | Matched non-beta accounts |
|---|---|---|
| Self-reported dispatcher hours saved per week | 4.1 | — |
| Change in jobs scheduled per dispatcher-hour vs the prior 12 weeks | +11% | +2% |
| 90-day renewal rate | 97% | 93% |

- Beta accounts volunteered; they are larger (8.1 seats on average) and more active than the base.
- Usage is concentrated: the top 10% of beta accounts generated 58% of all AI requests.

**Table 2. AI requests per account per month (beta)**

|  | Requests per month |
|---|---|
| Median account | 1,900 |
| Mean account | 3,600 |
| Mean of the top 10% of accounts | 14,500 |

- Model inference cost: $0.009 per request under the current provider contract, fixed through December 2027.
  The provider's list prices fell 35% over the past 12 months.
- Running the feature also needs about $0.6M a year of platform, evaluation and support cost.

## 6. Pricing evidence

- **Survey** (October 2026, 610 customer admins): at $149 per account per month, 46% said they were "likely" or
  "very likely" to buy Copilot.
- **Paywall test** (last four weeks of the beta): 120 beta accounts were offered Copilot at $149 per account per
  month after the free period. 17 accounts (14%) bought it. Accounts that bought averaged 6,800 requests a month.
- **Tier option:** a new "Pro" plan that includes Copilot, priced $12 more per seat per month than Core. When
  Brightwork last launched a higher tier (2023), 33% of accounts moved to it within a year.

## 7. Competitor evidence

- **Routewise**, the closest competitor, launched AI scheduling **included in its Pro plan** in September 2026.
- Brightwork's win rate in deals where Routewise competed fell from 44% (Q1–Q2 2026) to 37% (Q3 2026).
  Brightwork has about 2,600 qualified new-customer opportunities a year, and Routewise competes in about 60% of
  them; a new account averages 6.2 seats on Core.
- In Q3 2026 lost deals, 31% of loss notes mention AI features.

## 8. Customer evidence

**Table 3. Main reason given by accounts that churned, 2026 (n = 1,190)**

| Reason | Share |
|---|---|
| Mobile app reliability | 27% |
| Price | 22% |
| Missing integrations | 15% |
| Went out of business / sold | 14% |
| Switched for AI features | 6% |
| Other | 16% |

- Top feature request in the 2026 customer survey: "a reliable technician mobile app" (38% rank it first);
  AI scheduling is ranked first by 19%.

## 9. Costs

- Engineering: 14 engineers for two quarters at a fully loaded $210,000 per engineer-year.

## 10. Other material

- **VP Sales memo:** "31% of our lost deals cite AI, so Copilot would recover about a third of the deals we lose to
  Routewise."
- **Survey method note:** the October survey went to all 9,800 account admins; 610 replied (6%). Respondents average
  9.4 seats, against 6.2 for all accounts.

## 11. Uncertainties

- Whether the productivity gain holds beyond volunteers.
- How fast inference prices fall after 2027.
- Whether Routewise's AI is the cause of the lower win rate or coincides with its price promotion in Q3 2026
  (Routewise also offered 20% off the first year in Q3).

storyline.governing_thought: Ship the mobile rewrite first, then launch Copilot in Q4 2027 in a Pro plan at $12 more per seat with a usage allowance

exec_summary.text: Copilot demand is real but far below the internal case: at most $2.5M of add-on ARR, not $8M

sub_points.text: 14% of beta accounts paid $149, against 46% of survey admins who said they would
At the paywall rate, the add-on reaches at most $2.5M of ARR across 9,800 accounts

exec_summary.text: Copilot should wait for the mobile rewrite, whose delay puts nearly twice as much ARR at risk

sub_points.text: Mobile reliability drives 27% of churn, against 6% for AI features
Mobile first holds while the rewrite fixes at least 52% of mobile churn

exec_summary.text: Package Copilot in Pro at $12 more per seat, not a $149 add-on, with a usage allowance

sub_points.text: If 33% move up as in 2023, Pro adds $2.9M of ARR, $1.0M after costs
Margin holds at 75% only below about 5,300 requests per Pro account a month

exec_summary.text: Staff the rewrite in H1 2027, launch Pro in Q4 and track four gates toward 105% NRR

sub_points.text: Copilot build-out follows in Q3 and Q4 2027, with a Pro price test meanwhile
If the rewrite cannot fix half of mobile churn, launch Pro in Q2 instead

next_steps.action: Confirm the rewrite needs the 14 engineers only through Q2 2027 and fixes at least half of mobile churn; if not, launch Pro in Q2
next_steps.owner: CTO with Head of Customer Success

next_steps.action: Design Pro: $12 more per seat, a per-seat usage allowance and an overage rate; build metering into billing
Test Pro price and allowance on a random sample of non-beta accounts
Renegotiate the inference contract for 2028 to capture falling list prices
Brief Sales on the Pro launch date and keep current paying beta accounts served until then

sources.name: Brightwork briefing pack, Dispatch Copilot decision
Team analysis of the Brightwork briefing pack

constraints.item: Company gross margin must stay at or above 75%
constraints.effect: Pro keeps 76.0% at beta-mean usage but falls to 74.1% at paywall-buyer usage; the recommendation adds a usage allowance and a margin gate

constraints.item: 14 of 60 engineers for two quarters; launching Copilot delays the mobile rewrite by two quarters
constraints.effect: the central trade-off; quantified per quarter of delay and drives the sequence

constraints.item: One-off build cost of $1.47M (14 engineers × half a year × $210K)
constraints.effect: Pro contribution repays it in about 17 months

constraints.item: Inference at $0.009 per request fixed through December 2027; list prices fell 35%
constraints.effect: all 2027 costs at the contracted price; the price fall is upside from 2028 only and a reason a Q4 2027 launch loses little

constraints.item: Platform, evaluation and support cost of $0.6M a year
constraints.effect: deducted in contribution and counted in cost of revenue for the margin test; the CPO's $8M leaves it out
Pro reaches the 4 percentage point gap alone only if at least 26% of accounts move; made gate 1

constraints.item: Routewise's 20% first-year discount in Q3 2026 confounds the win-rate drop
constraints.effect: the competitive cost is labelled an upper bound

alternatives.option: CPO proposal: launch in Q2 2027 as a $149-per-account add-on
alternatives.why: the $8M rests on a 6% survey skewed to large accounts; actual paying conversion supports at most $2.45M, and heavy users make flat pricing thin-margin

alternatives.option: Launch Copilot in Pro in Q2 2027 and let the mobile rewrite slip two quarters
alternatives.why: per quarter, the rewrite slipping risks up to $544K of ARR against up to $281K from waiting on Copilot; waiting does give up about $257K of one-off Pro contribution per quarter (shown on the slide). The verdict reverses if the rewrite would remove less than 52% of mobile churn, so it is a January gate that switches the plan to a Q2 Pro launch

failure_threshold.driver: share of mobile-reliability churn the rewrite removes (timing); share of accounts moving to Pro (value)
failure_threshold.threshold: below about 52% churn removal, launching Copilot first in Q2 costs less; below 26% Pro migration, Pro alone misses the NRR target
failure_threshold.range: Pro new ARR $1.22M / $2.89M / $4.02M at 14% / 33% / 46% migration (contribution $0.09M / $1.03M / higher); 14% and 46% were measured at $149, so they bracket rather than bound Pro

consistency.headline: Ship the mobile rewrite first, then launch Copilot in Q4 2027 in a Pro plan at $12 more per seat with a usage allowance
consistency.fix: Titles call both delay costs upper bounds; Q4 2027 depends on the rewrite releasing the 14 engineers after Q2 2027, stated on the plan page and in next steps
